handDesc.handNote: Principal text and occasional darker or interlinear interventions are visible. No individual historical hands are assigned.

origin.p: The supplied library manifest dates the manuscript to 1001–1100. This catalogue date is not an attribution of the individual corrections.

surrogates.p: The two digital images each show a two-page opening. Left/right page labels identify the image position and do not assert medieval foliation. Later numerals 91 and 93 are visible on the right pages. Use is subject to the Gallica conditions linked by the source manifest.

projectDesc.p: All 84 verse lines inspected from enlarged manuscript images; no normalized edition used as transcription input. The text is an image-based draft that has received an independent second-agent reading; this is not human editorial approval.

correction.p: Witness readings are retained without silent emendation. Uncertain characters use unclear. Above-line letters use add; changes in ink use hi without asserting erasure or hand identity. Marginal annotations are encoded as manuscript notes, distinct from editorial notes.

normalization.p: Single manuscript display. Ordinary allographs, long s, and capitalization are represented with standard Latin characters; ligatures and abbreviation signs selected for retention are declared or encoded in abbr/expan choices. Spacing is editorially segmented. This is a legible diplomatic trial, not a facsimile-perfect inventory of every minute allograph or pen stroke.

punctuation.p: Significant visible punctuation is retained without adding systematic modern sentence punctuation.

segmentation.p: Each l represents one verse and one manuscript line. Even lines are indented following the page layout. The four physical page breaks occur before lines 1, 9, 37, and 65. Zones reuse the existing project image rectangles; those rectangles can include neighbouring ink and need not enclose marginal notes.

interpretation.p: Editorial observation and uncertainty notes retain reasoning and provenance. All 84 lines and the first-pass notes received a separate agent review. Only unresolved consequential readings use type review. Type uncertainty documents image limitations without requiring a reader decision. This does not constitute human editorial approval.

revisionDesc.change: First pass against all four physical pages, with source links and 84 line zones; submitted for independent second reading.

Independently inspected all 84 lines and four physical pages. Corrected the second conjunction in line 60, consistently encoded visible et ligatures, recorded the interlinear intervention at line 1, and replaced unsupported provisional groups at 36 with a qualified partial reading. Reviewed every first-pass note and retained two consequential editorial escalations.

div.head: Encoding and reading notes
div.note: The enlarged A is supported. At the second at a small u-like letter stands above the baseline t and a dot lies below it; this is now recorded as a qualified substitution rather than only darker ink. The exact form and relationship remain low-certainty. A small mark also occurs above the first letter of uotis in line 2; its precise correction history is not established.
The faint group in effecti supports retaining an uncertain c. The source image does not establish a deletion or its cause. No erased earlier reading is reconstructed.

The entire verse is visible: the short meæ-like group is followed directly by cicuta, with no room or visible separate word membra between them. Membra is therefore not supplied. The exact ligature in the short group remains uncertain, and li in gelida is darker.

The decorated initial is difficult to identify independently of the following ud and et sign. P is now explicitly low-certainty rather than an assured reading. No separate ah is recoverable with confidence; the ornament is not silently converted to one.

The added h after c is visible, but the baseline sequence and the small higher marks before candida remain difficult. The provisional lidetis has not been normalized to an expected name and numeral. The exact letters, possible second supralinear intervention, and word division remain a consequential unresolved cluster.

A second enlarged reading favors phenice over the first-pass phemee: the middle strokes appear to be n followed by i, and the final joined c/e-like forms carry a small lower curve. The full word remains low-certainty under unclear. Neither an unmarked confident reading nor the expected phoenicea is imposed.

The enlarged line supports a qualified beginning Forsitan impatiens, followed by sit and latus; the final recognizable group is meum. This replaces unsupported first-pass Cor stupet iners sic lassi demtam. The intervening i-like stroke and darker joined signs remain partly illegible and are not silently reconstructed as a complete phrase. The right-margin iis-like mark is retained separately. A secure complete reading remains unresolved.
The visible baseline supports Ad quale uidi tantum tetigique puellam. The marginal titici-like annotation remains unclear and unexpanded; the image does not establish a substitution relationship.

The right-margin annotation and adjoining strokes remain uncertain and schematically recorded. The baseline et ligature in ar& is now represented consistently with the other declared et signs. No marginal expansion or correction relationship is imposed.
The final nasal suspension over u is visible. The TEI durū/durum choice is supported, with the abbreviation shown in the single manuscript display.
The visible sequence supports Atque non tacita formaui gaudia mente. Word segmentation is editorial; the source is not silently changed to an expected quae reading.

A small interlinear character above the i in fixi is visible, shaped like an n/u form. The tentative added n remains low-certainty; it is not replaced by an asserted nasal bar and no correcting hand is assigned.

The baseline ramis and separate right-margin LANIS are visible. Both are retained without asserting deletion or formal substitution. The baseline aea remains as transcribed rather than automatically regularized to aeaea.

Visible et signs are consistently encoded as abbreviation/expansion choices at 40 and 45 (&iam), 51 (ar&), 52 (hab&), 61 (iuu& and cant&), 73 (&iam) and 76 (uid&). These replace silently expanded et strings in the first pass; the ordinary allograph policy remains unchanged.
The enlarged image reads nec uir after uixi; the first-pass neque uir is unsupported. Corrected to nec while preserving the earlier neque in the same line.
